How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to
allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the City’s website
as noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00 P.M. on the meeting
day will be forwarded to the City Council before the meeting for their consideration,
but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted after 4:00 P.M. will be
forwarded to Council but may not be received before the meeting.

Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
Public Comment.

   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, December 17, 2024

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Mayor Wu
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Wu, Vice Mayor Menchaca, Council Members Chan, Ding,
  Harrington

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council

  1. Minutes of the Special City Council Meeting of December 3, 2024.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as

  Recommended Action: Approval

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 17, 2024  2
   Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – NOVEMBER 2024

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2024-2025 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 24-35) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment
  Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s adopted
  2024-2025 Investment Policy.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for November 2024.

  D. DEVELOPMENT IMPACT FEE COMPLIANCE REPORT REQUIRED PURSUANT
  TO GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 66006 FOR FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024

  Pursuant to Government Code Section 66006, a local agency which levies a fee
  subject to Government Code Section 66001 shall make available to the public
  a report providing the information required by Government Code Section
  66006(b)(1) and shall review that information at the next public meeting no less
  than 15 days after the information has been made available to the public. The
  report was prepared in compliance with the applicable Government Code
  sections and is hereby transmitted for City Council approval. The report was
  publicly available on the City’s website beginning December 2, 2024. There is
  no fiscal impact with the acceptance of this report.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the attached Annual
  Development Impact Fee Compliance Report for Fiscal Year 2024-2024 in
  accordance with Government Code Section 66006.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 17, 2024  3
   E. FOUR-YEAR PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH GOLDEN BELL
  PRODUCTS, INC. FOR SEWER CHEMICAL TREATMENT SERVICES IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $76,700

  Under the Sewer Consent Judgement entered into between the City and the
  Regional Water Quality Control Board, San Gabriel is required to adopt and
  perform a complete sewer maintenance program. Staff seeks to continue the
  current annual preventative maintenance program with a chemical roach
  control agent. Golden Bell Products, Inc. has the sole source right for the
  application of Insecta, the only registered product of its type with an active
  ingredient labeled for use in sewer manholes. The four-year agreement with
  Golden Bell Products, Inc. shall not exceed $76,700. The adopted Fiscal Year
  2024-2025 budget includes funding for the first year of this Professional
  Services Agreement in the Sewer budget account 137-800-01-22-000, which is
  $18,200. The annual costs will fluctuate over the duration of the agreement.
  Future Fiscal Year funding will be planned and budgeted accordingly. Certificate
  of Insurance policies will be updated annually to ensure accurate coverage.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  a four-year Professional Services Agreement with Golden Bell Products, Inc. for
  chemical treatment services in an amount not to exceed $76,700.

  F. APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS TO PAY THE FINAL INVOICE FOR THE
  SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA EDISON (SCE) FACILITIES RELOCATION (RULE
  20B) PER AGREEMENT, IN THE AMOUNT OF $508,778.48

  In February 2020, City Council approved the Southern California Edison (SCE)
  Facilities Relocation Agreement (Rule 20B) to start constructing the
  underground overhead electric utility facility on Del Mar Avenue at Valley
  Boulevard. The final invoice is $508,778.48. Funding for this cost is not included
  in the FY 2024-2025 adopted budget. Staff is requesting an appropriation of
  $508,778.48 from the General Fund to account 122-800-15-96-743. Since the
  City is making the payment for the offsite improvements, there will be less of
  an offset of transient occupancy tax (TOT) in the future to reimburse the
  developer for the offsite improvement cost. In the future, if a loan agreement
  is entered, where the City would loan the funds to the developer and the
  developer would provide the funds to the City to make the payment, then this
  payment may not be viewed as an expenditure but rather a loan receivable.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 17, 2024  4
   Prior to this appropriation, the General Fund was projecting a $209,000 surplus.
  With this appropriation of $509,000, the General Fund will project a $300,000
  deficit which will be taken from the General Fund’s unrestricted reserves.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to approve
  a purchase order in the amount of $508,778.48 to pay the final invoice for the
  Southern California Edison (SCE) Facilities Relocation (Rule 20B) for the
  underground project on Del Mar at Valley Boulevard; and approve an
  appropriation of $508,778.48 from the General Fund to account 122-800-15-
  96-743.

  G. RESOLUTION NO. 24-69 AMENDING THE AUTHORIZED POSITION
  CLASSIFICATION AND SALARY SCHEDULE TO INCORPORATE THE 2025
  STATE MINIMUM WAGE INCREASE, UPDATE THE LIST OF AUTHORIZED
  PART-TIME LIMITED-SERVICE POSITIONS, AND ADJUST THE PART-TIME
  RECREATION AND AQUATICS PROGRAM POSITION PAY SCHEDULE TO
  LOCAL MARKET RATES

  On January 1, 2025, the State minimum wage will increase to $16.50 per hour,
  which represents a 3.13% increase to the current minimum wage. City-wide
  there are approximately 80 part-time limited-service employees who will be
  affected by the minimum wage increase, and there approximately 2 part-time
  Recreation and Aquatics employees who will be affected by the minimum wage
  increase and market rate adjustments to the part-time Recreation and Aquatics
  program positions. The minimum wage and market rate adjustments as
  described in this report are expected to have a combined annual cost impact
  of $45,145. The cost impact for Fiscal Year (FY) 2024-2025 is $22,573, with the
  General Fund incurring approximately $8,304 (36.8%) of the total increase. An
  additional appropriation of $14,269 in general funds and $8,304 in various
  other special funds is needed to cover the increase to part-time salaries in FY
  2024-2025.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 17, 2024  5
   Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-69, which
  amends the City’s authorized Salary Schedule by increasing the pay range of all
  part-time limited-service positions by the 2025 minimum wage rate increase,
  updating the list of part-time limited service positions by adding three new
  positions and retitling two existing positions, and adjusting the pay for the key
  part-time Recreation and Aquatic program positions to the local market rate,
  effective December 28, 2024, and increases General Fund appropriations
  $14,269 and various other special funds $8,304 to cover increase costs to part-
  time position salaries for Fiscal Year 2024-2025.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. FISCAL YEAR 2025-2026 COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT
  (CDBG) PROGRAMS BUDGET AND ALLOCATION (RESOLUTION NO. 24-58)

  Each Fiscal Year (FY), the City of San Gabriel receives an allocation from the Los
  Angeles County Development Authority (LACDA) for the Community
  Development Block Grant (CDBG) Program. For the FY 2025-2026, the City
  should expect to receive $297,581 (a 2.0% increase from the current year’s
  allocation) to be used toward developing viable communities and serving low-
  and moderate-income populations. The FY 2025-2026 CDBG Program and
  Budget Plan proposes to allocate the funding to the following programs: Youth
  Services Program, Code Enforcement, the Pedestrian Ramp Improvement
  Program, the Housing Rehabilitation Program, and a Graffiti Control Program.
  There is no fiscal impact for the current year, 2024-2025. The CDBG funding
  allocation estimate of $297,581 outlined in this report is for the 2025-2026
  Fiscal year and represents a 2.0% increase (approximately $5,841) from the
  current year allocation.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines, as a grant acceptance in
  of itself does not, does not have a potential for any adverse impacts to the
  environment.

  Prior to construction, separate environmental review of individual construction
  projects may be required.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 24-58 authorizing the allocation of Community
  Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds for Fiscal Year (FY) 2025-2026 from

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 17, 2024  6
   the Los Angeles County Development Authority (LACDA) for activities and
  projects described above and in Exhibit A of the Resolution.

  2. Carry over any CDBG funds unspent at the close of FY 2024-2025 and
  recognize the receipt of FY 2025-2026 CDBG Program funds awarded by
  LACDA to the City in the City FY 2025-2026 Budget.

  3. Recognize the receipt of an estimated $20,630 of CDBG funds from the Los
  Angeles County First District Supervisor’s Office if funds are approved by
  the Board of Supervisors for the After-School Sports Program for youth in
  grades 6-8.

  4. Allocate, in proportioned amounts, any FY 2024-2025 CDBG funds in excess
  of estimated funds to the Pedestrian Ramp Improvement Project, Code
  Enforcement Program, Graffiti Control Program, Housing Rehabilitation
  Program, and/or Youth Services Program.

  5. Authorize the City Manager to execute new contracts with LACDA for the
  allocation of FY 2025-2026 CDBG Program (subject to adjustment to reflect
  the actual allocation of funds to San Gabriel).

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. PURCHASE OF A MODULAR STRUCTURE IN THE AMOUNT OF $277,507.78
  PLUS $65,000 FOR UTILITY INSTALLATIONS AND SITE PREPARATION
  WORK AND DISCUSSION OF A MULTI-PHASE EXPANSION PROJECT OF
  THE SAN GABRIEL POLICE BUILDING [RESOLUTION NO. 24-71]

  This proposal introduces the multi-phase plan to renovate and expand the
  aging Police Department building, which was constructed in 1962 and is no
  longer able to adequately serve the men and women of the San Gabriel Police
  Department.

  Phase One: This phase will focus on the immediate needs of Department
  personnel and includes the proposed purchase of a newly-refurbished, modern
  modular structure to serve as the employees’ temporary locker rooms, showers,
  and restrooms in the amount of $277,507.78 plus $65,000 for utility installations
  and site preparation.

  Phase Two: This phase will include identifying the current and future needs of
  the Police facility with a phased development implementation plan. This report

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 17, 2024  7
   establishes the framework for this phase and opens up the discussion for the
  Police facility expansion.

  The cost to purchase the modular trailer is $277,507.78 and added to that cost
  is $65,000 for Public Works utility installations and site preparation for the total
  project costs. The funding for this project will include $100,000 in development
  fees restricted for Police facilities (171-751-00-99-175); $54,801 (16%) from
  Police facility development impact fees (124-751-40-99-175); and $187,000
  from the general fund (124-751-15-99-175). These funds were not included in
  the Fiscal Year 2024-2025 budget, and Resolution No. 24-71 is attached to
  appropriate the funds to the City’s budget.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends City Council approve the contract with Mobile Modular
  Management Corporation to purchase the proposed modular trailer and
  authorize the City Manager to approve a purchase order for $277,507.78.
  Additionally, staff recommends adopting Resolution No. 24-71 authorizing the
  use of funds to complete the project.

  B. RESOLUTION NO. 24-73 DECLARING THE RESULTS AND RECITING THE
  FACT OF THE SAN GABRIEL GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION HELD
  NOVEMBER 5, 2024

  On November 5, 2024, a General Municipal Election was held for the purpose
  of electing two members of the City Council. This item is to declare the results:
  The election of Tony Ding and Jorge Herrera Avila as members of the City
  Council for four-year terms. Funding for the election costs is provided in the
  approved Elections Budget for Fiscal Year 2024-2025 (Account No. 121-702-00-
  22-000). Final figures are not yet available as the invoice from the Los Angeles
  County Registrar-Recorder has not yet been received.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-73 reciting the
  fact of the General Municipal Election held on November 5, 2024, declaring the
  results and such other matters as provided by law.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 17, 2024  8
   C. RECOGNITION OF OUTGOING COUNCIL MEMBER JOHN R. HARRINGTON

  D. PRESENTATION OF CERTIFICATES OF ELECTION AND OATH OF OFFICE

  E. CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

  Pursuant to Government Code provisions, following an election, the City
  Council must take action to select a mayor and vice mayor. The terms of the
  current mayor and vice mayor may be extended to coincide with non-election
  year reorganization timing, or reorganization may proceed at this meeting.
  There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council extend the terms of Mayor Wu and Vice
  Mayor Menchaca to the April 1, 2025, City Council meeting.

  Alternatively, the City Council may direct the Chief City Clerk to proceed with
  the City Council Reorganization at this time.

 8. PUBLIC COMMENT

 9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

 10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

 11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

 12. ADJOURNMENT

  The regularly scheduled meeting of January 7, 2025, has been cancelled. The next
  regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, January 21, 2025, at 6:30 P.M.
  Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will be available
  on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website at
  www.sangabrielcity.com.
